title: The Circulatory System
seo_title: Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology: The Circulatory System Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: The circulatory system (heart, blood vessels and blood) carries oxygen and nutrients to body cells and removes wastes; it works with the respiratory system; exercise and healthy habits keep it healthy. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 5, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): the heart, blood vessels, blood, heart rate and exercise, and keeping the heart healthy. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The heart pumps blood around the body.
key_sub: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.
body_html:
How to think about it

The circulatory system is made of the heart, blood vessels and blood. The heart is a muscle that pumps blood. Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood back; tiny capillaries connect them.

Blood carries oxygen from the lungs and nutrients from food to every cell, and carries carbon dioxide and wastes away. During exercise the heart beats faster. Exercise, healthy food and not smoking keep the heart healthy.

Example

Which vessels carry blood away from the heart?

A for away

Answer: arteries

Example

Why does your pulse rate rise when you run?

Muscles need more

Answer: muscles need more oxygen

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the heart is on the left side only.
  • Thinking veins carry blood away from the heart.
  • Thinking blood only carries oxygen.

faq.q: How can you count your heart rate?
faq.a: Feel your pulse at your wrist and count the beats in one minute.

faq.q: Why is smoking bad for the heart?
faq.a: It narrows the blood vessels and makes the heart work harder.

items.q: What is the job of the diaphragm?
c: It moves down to help pull air into the lungs.
items.e: The diaphragm is a muscle under the lungs.

items.q: Why do doctors use a stethoscope?
c: to listen to the heart and lungs
items.e: Doctors listen for healthy sounds.

items.q: Which part of the circulatory system has this job: giving the blood oxygen and taking away carbon dioxide?
items.e: The lungs: giving the blood oxygen and taking away carbon dioxide.

items.q: Blood arrives at the right side of the heart. Where has it just come from?
c: the left side of the heart
items.e: Body → right side of heart → lungs → left side of heart → body.

items.q: What is the function of the gills?
c: Take in oxygen dissolved in water for fish.
Let gases enter and leave a plant.
Carries air from the nose to the lungs.
items.e: The gills take in oxygen dissolved in water for fish.

items.q: Which part takes in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide?
items.e: The lungs take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.

items.q: What is the main job of plasma?
c: carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body
carrying nutrients, water and waste as a liquid
letting oxygen and nutrients pass into the cells
items.e: Plasma: carrying nutrients, water and waste as a liquid.

items.q: What is the main job of the heart?
c: carrying blood away from the heart
helping blood clot to stop bleeding
carrying blood back to the heart
items.e: The heart: pumping blood around the body.

items.q: How does smoking harm the respiratory system?
c: It makes the lungs bigger and healthier.
It damages the lungs so they take in less oxygen.
items.e: Smoke damages the air sacs.

items.q: Blood leaves the right side of the heart. Where does it go next?
c: the left side of the heart
items.e: Body → right side of heart → lungs → left side of heart → body.

items.q: What is the function of the blood vessels?
c: Take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide.
Carry blood to and from all parts of the body.
Carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells.
Are where oxygen passes into the blood.
items.e: The blood vessels carry blood to and from all parts of the body.

items.q: What path does air take into the lungs?
c: nose or mouth → windpipe (trachea) → bronchi → lungs
items.e: Air travels down the windpipe.

items.q: Blood leaves the body's organs and muscles. Where does it go next?

the right side of the heart
items.e: Body → right side of heart → lungs → left side of heart → body.

items.q: What is the main job of red blood cells?

carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body
items.e: Red blood cells: carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body.

items.q: What is the main job of veins?
c: letting oxygen and nutrients pass into the cells
carrying blood away from the heart
carrying blood back to the heart
items.e: Veins: carrying blood back to the heart.

items.q: Which part of the circulatory system has this job: carrying blood away from the heart?
items.e: Arteries: carrying blood away from the heart.

items.q: Which part of the circulatory system has this job: carrying blood back to the heart?
items.e: Veins: carrying blood back to the heart.

items.q: What is the main job of white blood cells?
c: giving the blood oxygen and taking away carbon dioxide
helping blood clot to stop bleeding
carrying nutrients, water and waste as a liquid
items.e: White blood cells: fighting germs that cause disease.

items.q: Blood leaves the lungs. Where does it go next?
c: the left side of the heart
the right side of the heart
items.e: Body → right side of heart → lungs → left side of heart → body.

items.q: Which part of the circulatory system has this job: carrying nutrients, water and waste as a liquid?
items.e: Plasma: carrying nutrients, water and waste as a liquid.

items.q: Which part lets gases enter and leave a plant?
items.e: The tiny openings on leaves let gases enter and leave a plant.

items.q: Blood arrives at the left side of the heart. Where has it just come from?

items.q: Which organ systems work together to get oxygen to your muscles?

items.q: Which gas do we breathe out more of than we breathe in?

items.q: What does an asthma inhaler do?
c: It opens up the airways so air can flow more easily.
items.e: Medical technology helps people breathe.

items.q: Which organ pumps blood around the body?

items.q: Which substance does the blood carry from the intestines to all parts of the body?
items.e: The blood carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells, and carbon dioxide to the lungs.

items.q: Why does exhaled air make a cold mirror misty?
c: It contains water vapour that condenses on the mirror.
It is colder than the mirror.
items.e: We breathe out water vapour.

items.q: Which gas does the body get rid of when we breathe out?
items.e: Carbon dioxide is a waste gas.

items.q: Is blood leaving a hard-working muscle rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: What is the pulse?
c: the beat felt at the wrist or neck when the heart pumps blood
items.e: Each pulse beat matches one heartbeat.

items.q: Is blood in the right side of the heart rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?
c: Your muscles need more oxygen, so blood must flow faster.
items.e: Exercise increases heart rate.

items.q: Which gas does the body need from the air?
items.e: Cells use oxygen to release energy from food.

items.q: Is blood leaving the lungs rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: The blood carries water. In which direction?
c: from the small intestine to all parts of the body
from the intestines to all parts of the body
from all parts of the body to the lungs
from the lungs to all parts of the body
items.e: The blood transports substances around the body.

items.q: What is the function of the respiratory system?
c: to take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide
items.e: Breathing brings air into the lungs.

items.q: Which substance does the blood carry from the lungs to all parts of the body?
items.e: The blood carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells, and carbon dioxide to the lungs.

items.q: Is blood coming back from the body in the veins rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: Is blood in the left side of the heart rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: Air reaches the lungs. Where did it come from just before?
items.e: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs.

items.q: What are the three main parts of the circulatory system?
c: the heart, blood vessels and blood
items.e: Blood flows through blood vessels.

items.q: Air we breathe in passes through the nose. Where does it go next?
items.e: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs.

items.q: The blood carries oxygen. In which direction?
c: from the intestines to all parts of the body
from the lungs to all parts of the body
from all parts of the body to the lungs
from the small intestine to all parts of the body
items.e: The blood transports substances around the body.

items.q: Is blood in the arteries going to the leg muscles rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: Where does oxygen pass into the blood?
items.e: Tiny air sacs in the lungs pass oxygen to the blood.

items.e: Cells use oxygen and food to release energy.

c: It moves up and out as the lungs fill with air.
items.e: The lungs expand.

items.e: Add them and divide by 3: 288 ÷ 3 = 96.

items.q: How long does it take for the pulse to return to resting after exercise? How could you find out?
c: Measure the pulse every minute after stopping until it matches the resting rate.
items.e: Plan a fair investigation.

items.q: Where is carbon dioxide produced in the body?
c: in all the cells of the body
items.e: Cells release energy from food and make carbon dioxide.

items.q: Who first described how blood circulates around the body in 1628?
items.e: An English doctor.

items.q: Why should the pulse be measured three times and the average found?
c: to make the result more reliable
to make the heart beat faster
items.e: Repeating reduces errors.

items.q: Which of these is carried by the blood?
items.e: Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.

items.q: Why should you measure your pulse three times and find the mean?
c: to make the result more reliable
to make the heart beat faster
because one reading is always wrong
items.e: Repeats reduce the effect of mistakes.

items.q: Why do tadpoles use gills but adult frogs use lungs?
c: Tadpoles live in water; adult frogs breathe air on land.
Adult frogs live only in water.
items.e: Each matches where the animal lives.

items.q: Why do fit people often have a lower resting pulse?
c: Their heart is stronger and pumps more blood with each beat.
items.e: Exercise strengthens the heart.

items.q: Hauwa bubbled her exhaled air through limewater and pumped room air through another tube of limewater. What did she find?
c: Both turned chalky at the same time.
Only the room air turned it chalky.
Only the limewater with exhaled air turned chalky quickly.
items.e: Exhaled air has more carbon dioxide.

items.q: Why does a cut eventually stop bleeding?
items.e: Clotting forms a scab.

items.q: Ruth measured her pulse at rest, then right after skipping for 2 minutes. Why did she measure it at rest first?
c: to compare the result after exercise with the normal rate
items.e: The resting rate is the control.

items.q: Where is the heart found?
c: in the chest, between the lungs
items.e: The ribs protect the heart and lungs.

items.q: Which statement about the heart is correct?
c: It is a muscular organ that pumps blood all the time.
It is part of the respiratory system.
It takes in oxygen from the air.
items.e: The heart never rests.

items.q: Which body systems work together to bring digested food to the muscles?
items.e: Food is digested and absorbed, then carried by the blood.
